subject: APAC + EU connection throttle causing 503/504/429 — urgent customer escalation
messages:

Subject: High error rate across APAC/EU — 503/504 + 429 spikes

Hi team,

We're seeing a major increase in 503/504 and 429 responses for API calls routed from APAC and parts of Europe starting ~00:50 UTC. Throughput dropped ~40% and clients are getting timeouts. Sample request ids attached (request-id-sample.txt). This is impacting our checkout flow — several merchants have alerted.

Can you confirm if this is on your side or if we should fail over to our fallback provider? We need ETA and what mitigations are in flight.

Samantha

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-04-18T01:25:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Finexus APAC+EU 503/504/429 — triage & exec queue

Marcus / Evelyn — Finexus (large payments customer) reports widespread 503/504/429s in APAC and EU. They reported reduction in throughput and timeouts; they attached sample request ids. Customer is asking for ETA and mitigations.

Initial asks:
- Marcus: can SRE confirm whether this is LB/proxy throttling vs backend saturation? Share any short-term mitigations (circuit breakers/rate-limits) we can enact immediately.
- Evelyn: flagging this for exec awareness; if impact cross-regional, we'll need an on-call exec sync (CTO + VP Eng).

I see spikes on the edge dashboard (attached screenshot). Please triage and respond to customer with an interim update within 20 minutes. I will loop in Sales/CS if needed.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Engineering Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dashboard-screenshot.png (png)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T01:37:00Z
Subject: Re: URGENT: Finexus APAC+EU 503/504/429 — triage & exec queue

FYI — quick findings from initial triage:
- Edge LB (apac-edge-*) is seeing connection queueing and higher 502/503 return rates starting 00:48 UTC.
- Upstream pods are healthy by CPU/mem, but we have evidence of connection churn and repeated retries from client-side SDKs leading to connection storms.
- There's a sudden jump in 429s from our proxy layer consistent with upstream rate-limited backends (we're hitting a per-host connection cap on cloud provider LB).
- A small percentage (~3%) of ingress pods restarted between 00:52-00:56 due to transient ECONNRESET from the cloud provider, exacerbating capacity.

Immediate mitigation being applied (already in progress):
1) Enable temporary client-side aggregate rate-limit at the edge to reduce retry amplification (rolling out to APAC first).
2) Increase connection pool limits on proxy side and reconfigure health-check grace to avoid premature markings.
3) Reroute a subset of traffic to the dedicated serving pool for Finexus (canary) to restore throughput while we stabilize the public LB paths.

I've attached a small pod logs snippet and the incident runbook link. Will post further metrics in 15m.

Attachment: pod-logs-snippet.txt (text)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: caroline_choi@redwood.ai, matthew_cto@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T02:05:00Z
Subject: Exec summary: APAC/EU connection throttling impacting Finexus (P1)

Summary (for execs):
- Start: ~2028-04-18 00:48 UTC. Regions: APAC primary, spillover into EU 1-2 regions. Customer: Finexus (high priority payments account).
- Symptoms: Elevated 503/504 and 429 rates, increased end-to-end latency, ~35-45% throughput drop for affected tenants.
- Root-cause (current hypothesis): Cloud LB connection cap + transient upstream ECONNRESETs -> ingress pod churn -> retry amplification by SDKs -> proxy rate-limits trip.
- Immediate mitigation: Temporary aggregate rate-limit at edge, increase proxy connection limits, route Finexus traffic to dedicated pool.
- Next actions (0-2 hours): Stabilize traffic for Finexus; continue rolling mitigations across APAC; scale dedicated pool if necessary.
- Impact to customers: Several merchants on Finexus reported failed checkouts; broader customer surface is limited to tenants with APAC regional traffic.

Requesting exec approval for:
- Emergency capacity increase in APAC dedicated pool (expected cost hit for the hour).
- Short-lived SLA exception/credit conversation prep for Finexus if they request credits.

I'll coordinate the incident bridge. Marcus is leading remediation and Lauren will manage customer comms.

Attachment: incident-runbook.pdf (pdf)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finexus.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, cs-team@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T06:45:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate across APAC/EU — mitigation & next steps

Hi Samantha — quick update and timeline:

What we saw: transient connection limits on the cloud provider LB caused ingress pod restarts and an amplification of retries from several SDK variants, which in turn pushed the proxy layer into 429s and 503s for traffic routed from APAC and parts of EU.

What we did:
- Applied temporary aggregate rate-limits at the edge to reduce retry amplification.
- Increased proxy connection pool limits and adjusted health-check grace windows to prevent premature pod removal.
- Rerouted a portion of Finexus traffic to a dedicated serving pool; throughput for affected merchants increased to ~95% of baseline within 18 minutes.

Current status: traffic for Finexus is serving from the dedicated pool with reduced error rates. We're keeping the mitigations in place until midnight UTC tonight while we complete a root-cause verification and post-mortem.

Next steps:
- We will provide a full incident post-mortem with timeline and corrective actions within 48 hours.
- If you'd like, we can schedule a brief call with Marcus and our SRE lead to review the technical details and next steps for long-term resilience.

Apologies for the disruption and thank you for the quick flag — we know this impacts revenue-critical flows and are treating it as P1.

Sincerely,
Lauren Bishop
Engineering Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

If you see any residual errors, please reply with the latest request ids and timestamps and we'll prioritize them.
